description: The HUD window, which loads jarvis_hud.html — a page vendored from the backend folder and not written against this app. It holds NO pairing token (apps security audit M2): its requests to Jarvis go through Rust, which adds the token. `hud-link`: its reads, only from a fixed list (hud_proxy.rs `allowed_get`), its chat, the right/wrong mark on one answer, whether App lock and "Hide memory lists" are on (two yes/no answers, `get_lock_flags`, so its face never nods at a saved fact while either is on), and hide it again. `hud-voice`: `summon_push_to_talk`, which shows the quickbar with push-to-talk ready and records nothing, and `hide_quickbar`, the same hide the bar's own Escape uses, which the "Open the Jarvis bar" button beside the box sends when the bar is already on screen (the owner's ask of 2026-10-09: one button that toggles, labelled from what Rust says is on screen). `open-fix-place`: the settings gear the OWNER ASKED FOR on this window (2026-10-10, question 2 of docs/BARS-AND-SETTINGS-AUDIT-2026-10-10.md, where he chose to add it). Navigation only - it opens or focuses the Settings window at a named place, changes no setting and approves nothing, and the app lock still applies to whatever it opens. It is the same set the Jarvis bar's gear and the widget's gear already hold, granted for the same reason the widget needed it: a visible control wired to a command its window does not hold fails silently. `hud-approvals`: the card's own Approve and Deny, which the OWNER ASKED FOR on 2026-10-16 ("i should also be able to approve any card from the jarvis hud directly on my desktop and not need the jarvis widget or jarvis bar to do so"). That is ONE command, `decide_approval` - the same one the Jarvis bar and the widget call - so the stale-link refusal, the cut-off refusal, Windows Hello for the card the settings say needs it, and the App-lock rule (a window the lock covers approves nothing) all still apply; the page's own POST to /api/approve stays refused by the bootstrap's fetch shim, so this grant is the only way a decision can leave that page. It has no memory-write and no recording command. `hud-schedule`: the Reminders tab's two writes (2026-10-21, the owner's dedicated Reminders menu) - add ONE reminder, timer, alarm or to-do item, and change ONE job (snooze, add time, pause, resume, done, delete), both held on a stale link and both card-free because they only add or quieten. That set has NO list form and no delete-all: clearing a named list stays the Brain window's (Ruling 15). `focus-presets`: the left rail's five focus presets, added at the OWNER'S REQUEST on 2026-10-21 - that set's apply, `apply_focus_preset` (the BAR'S own command, the same one its "Use this preset" sends), which asks the PC and raises the PC's ONE switch_model card; nothing is approved here, and the page's own POST to /api/work/apply is refused by the bootstrap's fetch shim. Reading the list is hud_get's /api/presets, on the same fixed list as its other reads (the set's get-focus-presets read command is not needed by this page). So the worst a script running in this page can do is read what the HUD already shows, send a chat message as the HUD (any action it leads to still raises an approval card), mark an answer, open the quickbar, take it off screen, open Settings at a named place, or answer the one approval card whose id is on screen - held to Windows Hello, and refused outright while the link is stale or App lock is on. A fixed Stop everything control (`hud-stop`, owner-approved 2026-10-22) is the only new command this page may invoke: the same `stop_everything` the hotkey, tray and widget use. It cancels speech and the running turn, approves and starts nothing, and is never held on a stale link or App lock. Tauri IPC does work from this page despite its own CSP (Tauri falls back to postMessage), which is why this file, not the CSP, is the limit. The shell also pushes the event stream to it by evaluating a call to a feed the initialisation script defines. `hud-layout-read` (H1 of the editable-HUD design, 2026-10-21): the saved HUD layout, read by the injected bootstrap so the page can wear the owner's chosen preset - appearance-class, read-only, no approval card. There is deliberately no `remote` block anywhere: every window loads a bundled page. `hud-layout-write` (H2 of the editable-HUD design, 2026-10-22, owner-approved): the SAME appearance-class store, now writable by this page so its own Edit mode can save the layout the owner just arranged - `hud_layout.rs::sanitise` validates every write, a layout holds no private data, no approval card is raised, and this is the ONLY write command granted to this window (the app-lock, stale-link and approval rules above are untouched). `hud-personalities` (2026-10-27, the OWNER ASKED the Presets menu to list "the different personalities of jarvis that i can select"): the same `GET /api/manner` answer read for this window (`hud_personalities`), and ONE switch of ONE personality (`hud_switch_personality`, `POST /api/manner {"personality": "<id>"}`) - wording only, never what Jarvis does, asks, remembers or sends; NO card either way, and the switch is held on a stale link. Two narrow commands rather than a grant of the Settings window's `get_manner`/`set_manner`, which also carry the manner mode, the four dials and the custom personalities. There is deliberately no `remote` block anywhere: every window loads a bundled page.
